scenes.script_line: Welcome back to part 2 of the 6 core human needs. Let's begin by exploring the major development stages that each of us go through. According to sociologist Dr Morris Massey, the first stage is 0-7 and is known as the imprint period. During this time you were like a sponge forming an estimated 20 billion synapses in your little brain as you absorb vast amounts of information without really knowing how to make much sense of it all. 7-14 is known as the Modeling Period, where you begin to find people you admire and copy them taking on much of their beliefs and attitudes. scenes.script_line: During these developmental stages we learn either resourceful or unresourceful ways of getting our core needs met, which affects nearly everything we do in our lives. A resourceful way is simply a way that is good for you, good for others, and good for the greater good. It's a choice that is most optimal and sustainable for the long term. An unresourced way of meeting your core needs is one that is restrictive, offers you short-term gratification only and ultimately slows down your growth by keeping you dependent on a weaker choice.

Working hard to be skillful at your job, doing a quality service so that people truly appreciate and thank you for it. Being a giver of significance and genuinely appreciating those around you for all they do. Being thoughtful and attending to somebody else's need and receiving appreciation in return. Unresourceful, excessive bragging, letting everybody know just how wonderful you are in an arrogant way. Using your power to feel important as you threaten somebody in a weaker position to you. scenes.script_line: Next, let's explore vehicles for meeting our needs and how this could have saved me a lot of money. A vehicle is simply anything that helps you get your needs met. It could be a type of career path you take, the different relationships we have or an activity you engage in on a regular basis. When choosing your next career path or business venture it can be a very wise move to gauge how that choice will meet your six core needs. After all you will be spending a huge amount of your life doing it. So the more it meets your needs the more likely you are to do a great job and succeed.

scenes.script_line: For example, let's say you're deciding between two career pathways, option 1 and option 2. Simply take a moment to rate the two options from 1 to 10 in each of the six core needs. As you think about the two choices, work down your list, putting your score next to each of the human needs. Then add up your total and see how they compare. You may also wish to do this for your current job and relationships to gain a fuller sense of your present vehicles. The more vehicles you have that strongly meet your six core needs, the more fulfilled you are likely to be.
